EcoSwing delivered the world's first demonstration of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) direct-drive generator on a 3.6 MW wind turbine, using second-generation (2G) HTS wire coils to cut generator weight and rare-earth reliance in wind power. text: I keep coming across mathematics projects that bring knot theory to bear on physical field equations - studying how knots show up in the solution fields themselves, whether as knotted electromagnetic or magnetic field lines, knotted vortex lines and tubes in ideal fluid flows, or knotted nodal lines of quantum wavefunctions satisfying Maxwell's, Euler's or Schrodinger's equations. How do the projects working in this area differ in the physical systems and equations they focus on?
reference_answer: KNOTDYNAPP takes an electromagnetic and quantum-mechanical route: it proves that every knot type can occur as a stable closed field line of an electromagnetic field satisfying Maxwell's equations, constructs optical and quantum vortex knots as the knotted zeros of wavefunctions obeying Schrodinger and paraxial equations, and ties a knot's fiberedness to whether the magnetic field induced by a current through a knotted wire vanishes anywhere. GEOFLUIDS works instead in fluid mechanics and spectral theory, proving the Arnold-Moffatt conjecture on knotted vortex lines and Kelvin's conjecture on thin vortex tubes in Beltrami and steady Euler flows, and answering Berry's 2001 question by building Laplacian eigenfunctions whose nodal sets realize any knot type. FLUSPEC, a companion geometric-PDE program, targets smooth stationary solutions of the 3D Euler equations with chaotic trajectories confined in knotted vortex tubes of any topology, and studies vortex reconnection in the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. All three apply knot theory to solutions of physical field equations, but KNOTDYNAPP centres on electromagnetic field lines and quantum vortex knots whereas GEOFLUIDS and FLUSPEC centre on knotted vortex structures in incompressible fluid flows.
notes: Seeds: candidate cp2 vector-09 proposed KNOTDYNAPP(101023017)+BOPNIE(682537) via euroscivoc 'knot theory'. Reading BOPNIE(682537) shows it studies boundary value problems for nonlinear integrable PDEs; 'knot theory' appears once in a passing list of fields where integrable equations arise, and no knotted structure is studied - REJECTED as a euroscivoc false positive. KNOTDYNAPP is a genuine seed. Completeness sweep (non-embedding): run_sql objective LIKE '%knot%' returned the full 31-row universe; the only genuine knot-in-physical-field projects are KNOTDYNAPP(101023017), GEOFLUIDS(633152), FLUSPEC(862342); abstract-topology neighbours QuantGeomLangTFT(637618, TQFT knot invariants), LDTSing(101030083, algebraic/torus knots in 4-manifold surgery), MM-CAHF(893282, Heegaard Floer knot invariants), REFINV, OXTOP, GENERALIZED, ROGW all OUT (knots studied abstractly, no physical field); GOKNOT(796969, protein-backbone gordian knot via molecular dynamics) and MaCChines(787115, protein origami) OUT (discrete polymer, not a field-equation solution); euroscivoc 'knot theory' = {KNOTDYNAPP, BOPNIE}. Pooled adjudication (k=20, 37 candidates): IN KNOTDYNAPP (ranks L1/D1/H1/R1; EM field-line knots, quantum/optical vortex knots, fibered-knot vs induced magnetic field); IN GEOFLUIDS (L4/D2/H3/R2; knotted vortex lines/tubes in Beltrami/Euler flows, knotted nodal sets in QM); IN FLUSPEC (L2/D3/H2/R4; knotted vortex tubes of any topology in Euler flows, Gross-Pitaevskii vortex reconnection). OUT boundary candidates read in full: BOPNIE(682537) integrable-PDE BVPs; VORTSHEET(706283) 2D vortex sheets/patches, no knots; IPFLOW(725967) geodesic/Anosov flows and CFT, no knots; 3DWATERWAVES(678698) water waves over Beltrami flows, no knotted structures; HADE(669689) single vortex-filament equation/Talbot effect, no knot topology; GRAPHCPX(678156) graph-complex TQFT / rational homotopy of knot-spaces, abstract; TopMechMat(771503) 'knot' metaphorical (band-structure braiding); MM-CAHF(893282) abstract knot invariants. PANG (Pathogen and Graphene) builds graphene-based antibacterial matrixes by chemically functionalising them with antibacterial peptides and molecules such as menthol, then exploits the photothermal properties of rGO in suspensions and transdermal patches - among them a flexible skin patch that treats subcutaneous wound infections under photothermal irradiation - to kill pathogens non-invasively, while also probing the effect of these structures on the immune system and their mechanism of action. PEST-BIN uses graphene on two fronts: infection diagnostic kits built as disposable 'plug-and-play' chips of graphene functionalised with receptors that capture bacterial-surface biomarkers, containing only carbon and biodegradable polymers and now produced by the spin-out LayerLogic AB; and antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles and hydrogel/polymer coatings, loaded with antibiotics so that the resulting nano-weapon physically penetrates bacterial biofilms and delivers the drug inside them. Both therefore rely on graphene as an intrinsically antibacterial, functionalisable surface, PANG for light-triggered killing on the skin and PEST-BIN for sensing plus biofilm eradication.

text: Across the Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that include at least one organisation based in Italy, what kinds of approaches for monitoring volcanoes and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: The eight qualifying projects converge on making volcanic unrest measurable and interpretable in near-real time, along three complementary lines. New sensing hardware: NEWTON-g developed and field-tested the building blocks of a gravity imager, installing 4 MEMS gravimeters at Mt. Etna alongside an AQG-B absolute quantum gravimeter that it showed delivers continuous gravity data suitable for volcano monitoring, while reporting that COVID-19 delays meant the original 'gravity imager' idea did not come completely true; SiC nano for PicoGeo targets an optical fibre strain sensor built on a vacuum-encapsulated SiC thin-membrane resonator with picostrain resolution (10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients preceding eruptions, and reports first-stage work on SiC thin-film growth plus the first drilling of its test sites for strain-meter and seismometer installation; IMPROVE prototyped an automated gas-steam ratio sensor and demonstrated fibre-optic distributed acoustic sensing for volcano monitoring. Data-driven signal analysis and subsurface imaging: VULCAN.ears builds an automatic Volcano Seismic Recognition (VSR) system based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture to classify precursory seismicity in real time; PICVOLC integrated seismic, gravity and deformation data (GNSS, tilt, InSAR) with a physics-based 3D FEM inverse model and a new seismic tomography of Nevado del Ruiz, run with the Colombian Geological Survey's observatory (OVSM) and INGV - Rome, to locate and interpret sources of unrest; IMPROVE also combined seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical observations with machine learning to image magma storage at Krafla and Mount Etna. Simulation, early warning and observatory integration: ChEESE prepared exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic hazard assessment, running daily ensemble ash forecasts operationally during the La Palma eruption for PEVOLCA and civil protection; ARISE2 delivered a Volcano Information System (VIS) and near-real-time Volcano Infrasound Early-Warning (VIEW) notifications that infer ash plume height and mass eruption rate from infrasound signals; EUROVOLC networked volcano observatories and research institutions and opened virtual access to modelling and assessment tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.

text: Among the SME Instrument phase 1 projects classified under viticulture, how do the ones that build on a producer's own naturally occurring organisms, rather than on bought-in standard cultures, put those organisms to work in making wine?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle = 'viticulture' AND p.fundingScheme = 'SME-1' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the 14 SME Instrument phase 1 projects tagged viticulture take this route, and both make the producer's own resident biology the source of a wine competitors cannot replicate. MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) treats a winery's own bio-imprint as a commercial asset: it genetically selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts of different strains, so a house can keep dependable, robust fermentation and still bottle singular wines, the firm's stated aim being to recover the old diversity of wines without giving up modern production technology. Eternum works from the vineyard outwards: Bodegas Langa, with 150 years of winemaking expertise, profiles the vineyard's own microbiology and uses that profile both to draw up a highly specific low-impact pest control plan and to pick the site's own fermentation yeasts, then matures the wine together with those yeasts in a purpose-designed container that mimics the shape of a maturation deposit, so nutrients the organisms yield keep enriching the wine inside the bottle. The shared move is to replace a bought-in standardised input with an on-site biological one, LEV2050 packaging it as a technology any winery can buy and Bodegas Langa applying it to its own estate's production.

text: An EU fellowship set out to make simulations of the chemistry of heavy elements affordable, because the electrons there move fast enough that Einstein's corrections matter. What did that project report about how those corrections change the average distance between one electron and another?
reference_answer: The project is ReReDMFT (891647), which extended Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory to cover relativistic effects so that compounds of heavy elements could be simulated at an affordable cost. text: How do EU-funded projects approach tax evasion that operates through the links between firms - the companies a business buys from, sells to or shares owners with - rather than being the act of a single company on its own?
reference_answer: Two projects approach tax evasion as something produced inside business relationships rather than by one firm acting alone. DEVTAXNET starts from the claim that the most common and hardest-to-detect forms of evasion involve interactions across firm networks, which earlier work missed because it had mostly considered taxpayers as isolated units; it sets out to study, using unique administrative datasets from Chile and Ecuador covering networks of supply chains and of joint ownership structures, profit shifting by multinational firms to low tax jurisdictions, profit shifting and tax collusion among firms within the same country, and how the tax compliance of local trading partners of foreign-owned firms is affected. AnthroTax takes the same idea into ethnographic fieldwork in Croatia, studying how practices of tax evasion play out between family winemakers in Istria and a massive agribusiness conglomerate with which they do business, and frames the arrangement as 'hostage barter', through which corporate tax evasion is enacted as an apparent 'natural' feature of everyday business in a predatory economy. In both, the trading relationship itself is the unit of analysis - approached through firm-to-firm transaction data in one case and through the weaker partner's experience in the other.
notes: Seeds: 758984 DEVTAXNET and 101026736 AnthroTax, taken from cp5 candidate vector-42 (tax evasion). Drift check re-executed the candidate SQL (objective/title ILIKE '%tax evasion%') -> same 4 ids: 693402, 748062, 758984, 101026736. text: What have EU-funded research projects learned about how the judges at the global courts that put individuals on trial for the gravest crimes of war and mass violence understand their own role in shaping the law through their rulings?
reference_answer: Two projects speak to this. INCRICO interviewed judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and found that they see their duties as going well beyond applying recognised rules of law: they also treat fact-finding, dispute settlement, law-making, case management and governance - and, to a lesser degree, protecting the interests and values of the international community - as part of their judicial function, and these self-understandings feed back into the Court's deliberations, the drafting of its judgments and its use of separate and dissenting opinions. EaRL asked the same question of the wider international criminal bench, combining a systematic reading of all 240 available judgements of international criminal and hybrid courts (the ICC, the ad hoc Tribunals for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) and Rwanda (ICTR), and the Special Court for Sierra Leone (SCSL)) with over 40 in-depth interviews with judges, civil-society staff and government representatives, and traced empirically how routine practices of legal interpretation come to produce new legal meaning. Taken together, the two projects describe a bench that regards developing the law as one of its own achievements, and both look outward as well - INCRICO at how the Court's judgments are received as authoritative, EaRL at how a wider interpretive community of government officials, NGOs and other international courts takes up those decisions.

text: How do the aims differ between projects that study the woodwork of ships that sank centuries ago - what does each team hope those old ship timbers can tell them?
reference_answer: Both projects read the wood of ships that went down centuries ago, but they ask opposite kinds of question of it. ModernShip Project works on the structural remains of 16th-century wrecks of Mediterranean build - Mortella (1527, France) and Santiago de Galicia (1597, Spain), alongside the already documented Lomellina and Calvi I - in order to draft, for the first time, a Mediterranean technical model of how such ships were put together and to set it against the better-known Atlantic one, so that the continuous exchanges and technological transfers between the two nautical spaces can be described. TIMBER treats ship timber instead as precisely dated evidence about a resource: tree-ring work on the Swedish warship Vasa, built in Stockholm in 1628 and sunk on her first voyage in Stockholm Harbour, confirmed timbers from at least four distinct sources, including a Baltic and a west Swedish source, alongside purchase records naming eastern Sweden, Riga, Koenigsberg and Amsterdam, showing that even in heavily forested Sweden timber was imported from abroad. On the Boele Ship, a wreck dated to the 1380s found in the river Skienselva in southern Norway that sank with a cargo of whetstones from Eidsborg, every timber analysed - the keel included - came from the southern Baltic around the mouth of the Vistula River, which TIMBER reads not as evidence for the transport of timber but as a ship built at the Vistula mouth; both cases feed its account of the maritime timber trade from c. AD 1100 to 1700, with felling dates and regions of origin. The difference is what the wood is evidence for: for ModernShip it is evidence of design and construction practice in two coexisting technical cultures, for TIMBER it is evidence of where trees were felled, who traded them and how timber moved.

text: Some EU projects build solar-fuel photoelectrodes out of carbon nitride rather than a metal-based semiconductor, so they have to work out how to make the material themselves. How do those projects differ in the routes they use to produce and deposit the carbon nitride layer?
reference_answer: MFreePEC works bottom-up from the molecule: it encodes the composition of a family of metal-free CNX materials (X = P, B or S) into supramolecular precursors, uses the stable intermediate melem to synthesise CN photoanodes in the 5-20 min range at higher temperatures, and gets the layer onto transparent conductive electrodes by electrophoretic deposition, ultrasonic spray of precursors, doctor-blading, dip-coating and added precursor vapour pressure during calcination - a porous carbon-nitride photoanode containing reduced graphene oxide and a nickel-iron oxyhydroxide oxidation co-catalyst held photocurrents exceeding 0.45 mA/cm2 at 1.23 V vs. NHE for more than 35 h. CALSOL instead pits two whole synthesis routes against each other for its carbon-based artificial leaf - the traditional thermal polycondensation route and a plasma polymerization route - and its headline result is negative about the traditional one: the product of thermal polycondensation of melamine is not graphitic carbon nitride but a defective melon structure that degraded considerably during photoelectrochemical experiments, with a flatband potential drifting from approx. -1.5 V vs. Ag/AgCl to -1.8 vs. Ag/AgCl across pH. The contrast is therefore between engineering precursor chemistry and deposition method to build a durable working photoanode (MFreePEC) and testing whether an established preparation route yields a usable carbon nitride photoelectrode material at all (CALSOL).

text: Several EU projects set out to turn software that writes music by itself into something they could sell. How did they differ in what that software was meant to do for its intended users?
reference_answer: I2C8 turned the Lrn2Cre8 FET project's machine-learning work into a digital audio workstation plug-in for chord sequence generation, pitched to electronic musicians, producers and DJs as a 'musical sketchpad'; it deliberately stays small - predominantly sequences of up to eight chords - because its stated aim is to 'inspire' for composing, not to deliver complete compositions. AIVA, an AI that trained itself on 30,000+ classical music pieces, went the other way and offered content creators finished royalty-free soundtracks 'in the matter of seconds, and at the touch of a button', transitioning from a service to an embeddable Music Engine plus an API that lets third-party developers create hundreds of hours of soundtrack music, and it validated commercial feasibility by testing users' response and willingness to pay for the Music Engine public beta released in the second half of 2019. CALMUSgaming, from the Icelandic SME ErkiTónlist and built on its CALMUS technology, targeted computer games instead: its report says the software generates new background music as the game evolves, with minimal contribution from the composer, saving up to 90% of the time devoted to music composition, and the funded work was a feasibility study covering technical scope, markets and competition, a patent search and a 5-year financial forecast. FlowMachines, a PoC of the ERC Flow-Machines project, treated musical style itself as the asset to sell and set out to build a style manipulation prototype for the music synchronization business - music composed to be synchronized to existing media such as advertisements, movie music or video games - but its report concludes that 'Direct commercial exploitation of AI technologies per se is no longer a profitable route', that the team shifted to producing, distributing and monetizing content by the music industry's 'traditional means', and that they convinced top executives of a major music label to create a dedicated label specialized in the production and dissemination of music composed with AI technologies; on the legal side it catalogued the copyright issues in a report but 'considered that it was not worth addressing the issues raised by each copyright type'.

text: Which EU-funded projects study how companies and business groups try to influence the policies and regulations that governments adopt?
reference_answer: EU-funded research on this question sits mostly in political economy, and it covers both who does the influencing and what it achieves. Several projects put firms at the centre of trade rule-making: PROSPER studies firms that 'mobilize politically across global trade networks and influence trade policymaking in the European Union' and reports that because 'particularly resourceful firms are able to carry their political demands to policymakers, interest representation might be skewed in their favor'; TRASC builds a firm-level dataset of lobbying on the ratification and content of free trade agreements and on antidumping measures; DIA reports that the effect of industry lobbying on international rule-making depends on whether industries across countries share common or conflicting interests. Other projects work on domestic policy: BUSWEL compares the policy positions and strategies of business interest groups in Denmark, Sweden, Germany, Austria and the United States and, as delivered, focused on three policy fields - corporate taxation, inheritance taxation and wage bargaining - finding that the responsiveness of governments to business demands depends on the policy at hand and on the types of firms represented; MILO models how polluting firms' incentives to join a lobby group shape a policy maker's choice of environmental policy instrument; BIZPOL maps corporate political activity, 'all non-market activities by companies when they engage with governments and policy-making more broadly to advance their interests'. The set reaches further sectors and periods: POWERSHIFTS finds that 'firms in centralised systems have actively opposed policies that facilitate increased decentralisation' and that 'incumbent generators wield significant influence over energy policy processes'; MIGPSC asks how private security actors and the defence industry shape European migration management policy; GRIP-ARM asks how business power shapes the design of industrial policies in resource-rich countries; EFTA DEVELOPMENT traces how non-state actors including business lobby groups shaped EFTA's policies and priorities between 1958 and 1992; EURECON studies the influence of non-state actors including commercial banks and big business on European economic decision-making; and ClimActiv and CORPORATOCRACY treat corporate lobbying and corporate political power as questions of democratic legitimacy rather than of measurement.

text: What separation-management approaches for drone traffic have European U-space projects developed themselves - their own methods for keeping drones apart and resolving conflicts - as opposed to demonstrating separation services supplied by others?

pooling_evidence.note: single pooled run at k=40 over the final wording; 57 distinct pooled projects = 9 accepted-from-pool + 48 rejected. 776293 GAUSS is gold but retrieved by no condition at k=40; its provenance is the completeness sweep, recorded here rather than folded into the pooled arithmetic. hybrid_rerank returns 20 projects (reranker stage cap), the other three conditions 40.

reference_answer: European work on U-space separation splits between designing the separation service itself and validating deconfliction technology in flight. BUBBLES formulates a U-Space advanced (U3) separation management service at TRL3, computing UAS collision risk so that separation minima and methods - procedural, tactical self-separated or tactical ground-based - can be derived from a stated probability of collision. USEPE studies separation methods for demanding environments such as cities and applies machine learning to automate safe separation and deconfliction while holding airspace capacity. Metropolis 2 treats airspace design, flight planning and separation management as interdependent at high traffic density, comparing concepts that differ in how separation is performed (strategic/tactical, ground/air) by simulation before a real-world demonstration, while DACUS embeds separation management in a Demand and Capacity Balancing process and searches for the optimal balance between on-board separation intelligence and U-space separation service intelligence. LABYRINTH takes the centralised route, computing 4D paths for drone swarms so trajectories do not collide. On the technology and demonstration side, CLASS matured ground-based tracking with tactical deconfliction tools that suggest new conflict-free trajectories; IMPETUS tested tactical de-confliction in which virtual weights attached to each drone define the separation criteria, giving dynamic separation; TINDAiR demonstrated AI-based tactical deconfliction with a detect-and-avoid service over VTOL flights; GOF2.0 validated an architecture for highly automated real-time separation assurance in dense urban airspace; and GAUSS approaches coordination among UAS through Galileo-EGNOS precise positioning plus tactical deconfliction services in its UTM system.
notes: Membership criterion is now STATED IN THE QUESTION: a project is gold iff its own stored text shows it developed or validated its own method for keeping drones apart or resolving conflicts between them (separation minima, strategic or tactical deconfliction, conflict detection and resolution) within U-space/UTM; a project that only demonstrates or consumes a separation-type service supplied by partners is excluded by the question's own words ('as opposed to demonstrating separation services supplied by others'), as is on-board sensing hardware and manned-aviation separation work. The earlier 'large numbers of drones' qualifier was dropped because gold members TINDAiR (largest exercise: 'Deconfliction between an autonomous drone, an eVTOL carrying a passenger and a manned helicopter') and GAUSS ('4 UTM coordinated RPAS') do not satisfy it. text: Which projects are aimed specifically at preventing, or detecting at an early stage, the skin and tissue damage that long periods of unrelieved pressure inflict on bedridden or wheelchair-bound patients?
reference_answer: Six H2020 grants in this corpus are aimed at this problem, and most are sensing-plus-prevention systems rather than treatments. i-LiveRest (696939) and its successor grant LiveRest (830134) put impedance, pressure, temperature and humidity textile sensors on a wheelchair or mattress to score Tissue Viability in real time and then trigger the prevention strategy that suits the user and context; their target group is Spinal Cord Injury patients, 85% of whom develop such an injury. Qone (735302) does the equivalent for bedridden patients with a pressure-relieving mattress carrying temperature and pressure mapping sensors feeding a personalised risk-score algorithm, claiming roughly a 75% reduction in new cases. The two JUMPAIR grants (709595, 783594) build a smart anti-decubitus mattress system that remotely tracks known ulcer-activity biomarkers to raise early alerts to the hospital. STINTS (811965) is the research and training strand: it studies the biomechanical and biochemical pathways by which prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity, in order to improve preventative aids such as mattresses and insoles, early-stage diagnosis through non-invasive biomarkers and sensors, and ultrasound therapy.

text: Which projects are developing chips or other dedicated hardware in which artificial neurons compute by firing brief pulses at each other, the way nerve cells do?
reference_answer: A cluster of H2020 projects builds computing hardware in which the signals are neuron-like pulses rather than clocked digital arithmetic. NeuRAM3 proposed to fabricate a chip implementing a neuromorphic architecture supporting spike-based learning, in FDSOI at 28nm design rules with RRAM synapses; MeM-Scales works on analog spiking microprocessors whose memory devices cover timescales spanning up to 9 orders of magnitude; SYNCH couples the brain of a living animal to a silicon neural network of spiking neurons on a chip through neuromorphic synapses; ULPEC connects a neuromorphic event-based camera to a Spiking Neural Network with memristive synapses; ChipAI builds resonant-tunnelling nanophotonic sources and detectors that fire and detect neuron-like light-spiking signals at >10 GHz per spike rates; NEPSpiNN puts event-based spiking processing of surface EMG into a compact ultra-low power neuromorphic chip; BeFerroSynaptic packaged TEXEL, a 9mm x 9mm neuromorphic chip carrying 180 adaptive-exponential integrate and fire (AdExp-I&F) neurons fed by ferroelectric synaptic devices; and TEMPO and ANDANTE develop the underlying technology and hardware platforms (integrate-and-fire engines, emerging memories, 3D integration, edge SNN chips). The same set also includes NANOINFER, whose intelligent memory chips combine digital CMOS logic with spiking neurons circuits, Fun-COMP, whose nanoelectronic and nanophotonic building blocks implement spiking neural networks in hardware, NeuroAgents, which fabricated the DYNAP-SE2 mixed-signal Spiking Neuronal Network processor for neuromorphic robotic agents, and SOFT, which designed, fabricated and tested a magnetic domain-wall spiking neuron and used a magnetic neural network to recognise patterns from human voice converted into spikes.

text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.

text: Which projects are engineering CAR T cells to attack solid tumours?
reference_answer: Eight H2020 projects engineer chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells against solid tumours, the setting where CAR therapy has lagged behind its success in blood cancers. Several build new CAR specificities: AngioCAR aims CAR T cells at extracellular vimentin (eVim) on the tumour vasculature, SweetCAR at sialic-acid carbohydrate neoantigens on carcinomas, and CARsen at senescent cells in solid tumours and senescence-associated disease. Others attack the hostile tumour microenvironment instead - Exh-Res-CART and Tex-Mex both work on T-cell exhaustion (biochemical and biomechanical triggers respectively), TRAP-CART uses gene-modified blood-derived cells in the tumour microenvironment to switch on programmable CAR T cells locally, with melanoma as its model cancer, and EnhancemenT modulates ZFP36/ZFP36L1 RNA-binding proteins in CAR-T cells to raise their in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity. CARAT is the platform case: automated GMP-compliant manufacture of CAR-modified T cells together with innovative CAR designs, intended to serve patients with incurable solid tumours as well as haematologic malignancies.

text: A project set out to work out how often rivers across Spain and neighbouring parts of southwestern Europe burst their banks and caused serious damage, going back hundreds to thousands of years before gauge measurements began, by reading the bands of mud that had settled on lake bottoms. How did its researchers work out which of those buried bands had been laid down by such an event?
reference_answer: The project (FLOODARC) worked from sediment cores and geochemical and chronological datasets that were already available for the studied Iberian sites: it started with descriptions of those cores, then prepared thin sections and applied a state-of-the-art protocol that combined detailed microfacies analyses with geochemical analyses to identify the flood layers. The flood records it analysed span from the last centuries in the Western Ebro Basin (NE Spain) to the last 26000 years in NW Spain.

text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.

text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships classified under cognitive neuroscience and hosted by an organisation in the Netherlands, how do the ones that act on the brain from outside the head, rather than only measuring it, use that to test whether a particular brain area or the pace of its activity is genuinely doing the work?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' AND e.euroSciVocTitle = 'cognitive neuroscience' AND o.role = 'coordinator' AND o.country = 'NL' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Three of these fellowships intervene rather than only observe, and they split by direction. ORCA drives activity with transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), synchronising rhythmic activity between two attention-related regions while recording EEG and, in a second study, fMRI; it found no effect on spatial attention in 23 participants but a frequency-specific effect on vigilant attention in 101 participants, which it reads as the first causal evidence for the medial frontal cortex in vigilant attention. NERHYMUS and MemoryBasedPercepts instead damp a named region with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and ask whether performance suffers: NERHYMUS uses neuronavigated TMS combined with EEG to down-regulate the supplementary motor area (SMA) and test whether that region is really necessary for processing rhythm in speech, and a preliminary analysis of 9 non-musician datasets suggests the TMS does affect processing of regular rhythm in poems. MemoryBasedPercepts first characterises memory-based percepts with fMRI and MEG and then applies TMS to test whether activity of visual cortex is causally necessary for them, reporting that it is - those visual regions are directly implicated in producing knowledge-driven perception.
notes:
FILTER RATIONALE. Three predicates, every one a stored column and every one stated in the question: p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (the MSCA individual-fellowship family, which includes MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST and MSCA-IF-GF), e.euroSciVocTitle = 'cognitive neuroscience', and a Dutch coordinator. 17 survivors - inside filter-synthesize's 5-20 window and far under the 200-row enumerability ceiling. Intermediate counts re-executed this pass: MSCA-IF x cognitive neuroscience = 108 before the country predicate; MSCA-IF x NL coordinator = 625 without the leaf.

ONE-READING CHECK. euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%cognitive neuroscience%' returns exactly ONE row - path 'natural sciences/biological sciences/neurobiology/cognitive neuroscience', 201 projects corpus-wide - so the title reading and the subtree reading select the identical set and the scope has one executable reading.

WORDING ROBUSTNESS. 'hosted by an organisation in the Netherlands' cannot be read two ways here: the coordinator reading (role='coordinator' AND country='NL') and the any-participant reading (country='NL', any role) both return the identical 17 ids - EXCEPT in both directions returns 0 rows. The recorded SQL uses the coordinator reading.

ADJUDICATION - EXHAUSTIVE. S=17 <= 20, so every survivor was read and adjudicated this pass; no pooling gap exists. The three IN projects were read at full payload (objective + all report sections); the OUTs from objective/teaser.
IN 702402 ORCA - applies transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to synchronise rhythmic activity between two attention regions, explicitly to 'investigate the causal role of neural oscillations in attention'; reports a frequency-specific effect on vigilant attention and a causal role for medial frontal cortex.
IN 794455 NERHYMUS - 'will employ transcranial brain stimulation (TMS) to disrupt pre-SMA involvement in rhythm perception in order to examine whether this region is really necessary'; report confirms neuronavigated TMS, combined EEG-TMS, and a preliminary SMA effect on regular rhythm in poems.
IN 101033489 MemoryBasedPercepts - 'I will use Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) to test whether activity of visual cortex is causally necessary'; report confirms the stimulation was run and the necessity established.
OUT 657255 NeWMaBIL - MEG only; measures oscillatory correlates of working-memory control in aged bilinguals, no intervention.
OUT 703493 NEUROBUKIMI - fMRI of emotional responses to virtual characters plus a questionnaire; observational.
OUT 704992 CraNOC - does perturb causally, but with viral optogenetic tools controlling the nucleo-olivary pathway inside the animal brain; not from outside the head.
OUT 705010 Detect and React - event-related potentials plus a driving simulator; measures detection and reaction, never acts on the brain.
OUT 706714 CONNECT - multi-modal molecular and magnetic neuroimaging of amyloid/tau/activity interaction; observational.
OUT 707727 AVISSO - EEG and fMRI, and it does test necessity, but by studying Parkinson's patients with dysfunctional basal ganglia; a patient-group design, not an applied intervention.
OUT 707865 Expectancy learning - EEG, MRI and Bayesian modelling of expectancy formation; observational.
OUT 791181 SOURCES - fMRI, EEG and eye-tracking on arousal and decision strategies; observational.
OUT 800046 NeuroPred - Event-Related Optical Signal, eye-tracking and MEG; observational.
OUT 841909 FromObjectsToScenes - fMRI and MEG on object-constellation processing; observational.
OUT 843379 ResonanceCircuits - does perturb causally, but by optogenetically silencing GABAergic interneuron classes with implanted laminar probes in awake mice; the flickering light is a sensory stimulus, not an action on the brain, so it fails 'from outside the head'.
OUT 844734 ToMComputations - two fMRI experiments on Theory of Mind; observational.
OUT 101025627 MyeSync - subcellular patch-clamp, Ca2+ imaging and in vivo electrophysiology in animals; invasive recording, no transcranial intervention.
OUT 101030415 ReWoMeN - mathematical and deep-neural-network modelling of working-memory recall; no experiment on a brain at all.

BORDERLINES, STATED. 704992 CraNOC and 843379 ResonanceCircuits both intervene causally and would be IN under a looser reading ('perturb the brain'); they are OUT because the question says 'from outside the head', and optogenetics needs virus and implanted hardware. 707727 AVISSO tests necessity but by choosing a patient group rather than by acting on a brain. These three are the question's real discriminators and a reader has to resolve them from the text.

NON-EMBEDDING SWEEP. Over the 17 survivors' concatenated objective + report teaser/summary/workPerformed/finalResults, ILIKE on transcranial / TMS / tACS / brain stimulation / stimulat%. Six survivors matched anything; only 702402, 794455 and 101033489 matched a transcranial term. 843379 matched via 'stimuli' and 'optogenetic', 707865 and 791181 via 'stimulus/stimuli' only. The sweep found nothing the exhaustive read had missed.

FILTER LOAD-BEARING - three independent lines. (1) Unscoped pooled search on the final question text returned 25 distinct projects and NOT ONE of them is a survivor: with the filter dropped, retrieval does not reach the gold set at all. (2) SQL counter-example count: 132 projects corpus-wide name TMS or tACS in their objective; 129 fall outside the filter and exactly 3 fall inside - the 3 gold. (3) Named counter-examples, each read this pass and each failing exactly ONE conjunct: 725970 NATVIS (NL coordinator, has the cognitive neuroscience leaf, but ERC-COG) uses 'fMRI, MEG, and TMS' and tests 'causal interactions between scene- and object-selective pathways in visual cortex' - fails only fundingScheme; 799238 BetweenTwoBrains (MSCA-IF, has the leaf, UK coordinator) uses 'dual transcranial alternating current stimulation (dual-tACS)' to 'test the hypothesis that there is a causal link' - fails only country; 798619 TUNING-BRAKES (MSCA-IF, NL coordinator, no cognitive neuroscience leaf) is entirely about tACS as a 'non-invasive brain stimulation technique' probing 'the causal role of interactions between beta oscillations' - fails only the leaf. So every conjunct of the filter is individually load-bearing, not merely the filter as a whole.

TEXT LOAD-BEARING. No stored column records what method a project uses. The filter alone hands back 17 projects with nothing to separate them; which three act on the brain, what they target and what they concluded exists only in objective and report free text.

TERM_STYLE = paraphrase. The question avoids every distinctive term the gold texts use - transcranial, TMS, tACS, stimulation, oscillation, causally necessary, disrupt - and says instead 'act on the brain from outside the head', 'the pace of its activity', 'genuinely doing the work'. The scoped rank matrix agrees: 101033489 is absent from lexical entirely (dense 6, hybrid_rerank 8); 702402 is lexical 10 against dense 3 and hybrid_rerank 2; 794455 is lexical 8, dense 8, hybrid 9, hybrid_rerank 5. An earlier wording of this question used the word 'rhythm' and put 794455 at lexical rank 1; the word was removed because that was genuine term overlap, and the rank fell to 8.

SCOPED RETRIEVABILITY. All three gold appear in at least one condition's scoped top-k (above). Worth noting for the study: the top scoped hits are NOT the gold - 791181 SOURCES, 101025627 MyeSync and 706714 CONNECT outrank them - so retrieval alone does not settle this question; the survivors have to be read.

RUNTIME NOTE. src/retrieval/scoped.py's id-narrowing prompt whitelists fundingScheme and organization.country but NOT euroSciVoc, so at runtime the scoped path builds the scheme + country half (625 projects) and the 'cognitive neuroscience' constraint falls to retrieval. That is the intended division of labour and the same shape as hyb-01, hyb-03, hyb-07, hyb-08 and hyb-09.

EVIDENCE BOOKKEEPING. Adjudication is from the exhaustive read of all 17 survivors. pooling_evidence.pooled_candidate_count (14) and scope_size (17) come from the scoped pooled search, which was run for retrievability and the rank matrix; rejected_count (14) is the exhaustive read's rejections (17 - 3).

The rejected version's filter_sql was a free-text ILIKE device over concatenated title/objective/report fields whose survivor count of 7 was the output of that keyword search rather than of anything the question stated; its only question-stated predicate, fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%', matched 9,845 projects. Subject and gold are entirely re-derived here: the old gold four share no euroSciVoc leaf at all (659719 cognitive neuroscience, 888270 none of the neuro leaves, 892772 neurobiology, 898460 no euroSciVoc row whatsoever), so no stored-column filter could have reproduced them.

text: The European Research Council runs several different kinds of grant. For each ERC grant type in the H2020 data - the funding schemes whose code starts with ERC- - how long does a project last on average, in days from its start date to its end date (end date minus start date)?
gold_sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) AS n_projects, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day', startDate, endDate)),1) AS avg_duration_days FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC-%' GROUP BY fundingScheme ORDER BY fundingScheme
reference_answer: Seven funding schemes carry an ERC- code, and their average durations fall into a long band and a short one. The long band is the main research grants, 5.7 to 6.7 years each: ERC-SyG averages 2446.0 days (99 projects), ERC-COG 2099.9 days (2254), ERC-STG 2083.3 days (2771) and ERC-ADG 2082.5 days (1584). The short band runs from about 1.6 to 1.8 years: ERC-LVG averages 656.2 days (5 projects), ERC-POC-LS 610.4 days (158) and ERC-POC 576.1 days (967). The five ERC-LVG grants are support awards to external publishing initiatives (OAPEN, SciPost, Europe PMC) rather than research projects. No ERC project has a missing start or end date, so all 7838 of them are included.
notes: Group set is pinned in the question text to the ERC- scheme code, and the text also pins the metric to subtraction (end date minus start date), because an inclusive endpoint count returns exactly +1.0 day on all seven rows and results_match compares at 1e-6. Boundedness checked on two channels. (1) Scheme string: SELECT DISTINCT fundingScheme FROM project WHERE lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%erc%' OR lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%research council%' returns exactly the seven ERC- codes (ERC-ADG, ERC-COG, ERC-LVG, ERC-POC, ERC-POC-LS, ERC-STG, ERC-SyG). (2) Programme channel, the near-miss: SELECT p.fundingScheme, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day',p.startDate,p.endDate)),1) FROM project p JOIN legal_basis lb ON lb.projectID=p.id WHERE lower(lb.title) LIKE '%european research council%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 returns those seven rows unchanged PLUS an eighth group, CSA | 12 | 813.1 - ERC administration and communication contracts under the ERC programme part. The question's ERC- clause makes that eight-group reading unavailable. Duration is pinned to whole days deliberately: a months formula has two defensible variants (calendar month-boundary count vs days/30.44) giving different numbers. Null-date exposure is zero: the 12 corpus-wide projects with NULL startDate/endDate (structural finding sf-11) are all outside the ERC schemes - SUM(CASE WHEN startDate IS NULL OR endDate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 for every ERC- scheme, over 7838 ERC projects. ERC-LVG's five members were read directly (637529 ERC-EuropePMC-2-2014, 683680 ERC-OAPEN-2015, 810640 ERC-OAPEN-2017, 899590 ERC-SciPost-2019, 964352 ERC-OAPEN-2019) so the reference describes them from their titles, not by analogy to ERC-POC. Averages rounded to one decimal in the gold SQL. n_projects is context, not compared; answer_columns pins fundingScheme and avg_duration_days. No ranking asked or implied - sql_comparison=set.

text: Among Horizon 2020 projects that started on or after 1 January 2018, how many had at least one Italian organisation receiving more than 1 million euros of EU funding?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.projectID) AS project_count FROM organization o JOIN project p ON p.id = o.projectID WHERE o.country = 'IT' AND o.ecContribution > 1000000 AND p.startDate >= DATE '2018-01-01'
reference_answer: 478 Horizon 2020 projects with a start date on or after 1 January 2018 include at least one Italian-based organisation whose EU contribution exceeds 1,000,000 EUR. Those projects account for 548 such Italian participations, so a count of organisation rows rather than distinct projects overstates the answer as 548.
notes: Trap = entity grain (organization participation rows vs projects). Wrong query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM organization o JOIN project p ON p.id = o.projectID WHERE o.country = 'IT' AND o.ecContribution > 1000000 AND p.startDate >= DATE '2018-01-01' -> 548; gold with COUNT(DISTINCT o.projectID) -> 478. Corpus-wide drift check of the seed evidence reproduced: country='IT' gives 17,243 organization rows vs 7,899 distinct projects. organization.ecContribution is NULL for 7,658 unfunded MSCA 'partner' rows plus 142 others; NULL > 1000000 is not true, so unfunded participations are correctly excluded by the threshold. text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to do away with the lenses and reflectors added onto low-energy lamps by placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings - stacked layers, patterned surfaces and resonant cavities - so that the tint and the beam spread of the light are fixed by those surroundings rather than by changing what the particles themselves are made of?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it puts rare-earth nanophosphors inside engineered optical structures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, nanoimprinted corrugations and optical cavities - and shows that those surroundings alone set the chromaticity and the directionality of the device's output, 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', replacing the reflectors and lenses normally added as secondary optical elements. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'nanophotonics' (one-reading check: 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics' is the only path matching '%nanophotonics%', 62 projects) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-STG' -> 10 survivors, re-executed this pass. Runtime note: the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) can only filter the structural half ('ERC Starting Grant' -> fundingScheme='ERC-STG'); the nanophotonics topic is carried by retrieval, which is how the question is worded. LOW note on scope width: the enumerated survivor set is narrower than the runtime's executable scope (all ERC-STG projects), so ERC-STG projects tagged under other euroSciVoc leaves - e.g. 849229 CQWLED (nanocrystals / colors / optoelectronics) - are reachable at runtime but not enumerated here; CQWLED is excluded by the question's own words (see ADJUDICATION), so this is a recorded width note, not a gold gap. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 10 survivors read at objective+teaser, gold at full payload; re-adjudicated against the current wording): 715832 NANOPHOM IN - 'exploits new ways of controlling the emission characteristics of nanophosphors, surpassing the limits imposed by conventional optics', design 'based on multilayers, surface textures and nano-scatterers', and the report states the control comes 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', with reflectors and lenses named as the secondary optical elements being replaced. OUT: 637116 ENLIGHTMENT (photonic electrodes to enhance light ABSORPTION in thin solar cells, photodetectors, sensors); 639109 FLATLIGHT (visible-wavelength metasurfaces as ultrathin reconfigurable optical components and modulators, not emission from a lamp's emitting particles); 677470 SEAQUEL (cold structured atomic ensembles for quantum engineering of light); 679841 ORDERin1D (chirality-sorted carbon nanotubes, molecular filling and order); 714151 PSINFONI (particle-surface near-field interactions, optical and Casimir forces); 802682 MODES (nonlinear multimode processes in fibres, chips and nanoparticles); 802986 aQUARiUM (epsilon-near-zero rolled-up metamaterials for quantum light-matter interaction); 853500 NanoGraphy (plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic nanolithography); 948804 CHANSON (chiral semiconductor nanophotonics for molecular sensing). NEAR-MISSES EXCLUDED BY THE QUESTION'S OWN WORDS: 798697 NEXTLEDs is titled 'Chemical Engineering of Atomically-Flat Colloidal Quantum Wells' and works by synthesizing the emitters themselves - the mechanism the question explicitly rules out - and is MSCA-IF, failing the scheme filter too; 849229 CQWLED likewise guides 'chemistry and shape' of its nanocrystals, never opposes itself to lenses or reflectors (its foils are total internal reflection and EQE), and its 'layers' are the emitter superlattices rather than engineered surroundings. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text): 657434 PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST) satisfies the textual ask outright and ranks dense 1 / hybrid 1 - 'integrating novel optical nanostructures and emitters, such as colloidal quantum dots or nanophosphors ... preparation and processing strategies, based on surface textures and colloidal scatterers, to attain large area optical nanostructures ... precise control on the intensity, angular distribution and color quality of light emission' - and it fails the ERC-STG filter, so dropping the filter changes the answer. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records what a project does with light emission; the filter alone leaves 10 candidates. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question uses 'tint', 'beam spread', 'low-energy lamps', 'stacked layers', 'patterned surfaces', 'resonant cavities' and avoids the gold's distinctive vocabulary (nanophosphor, LED, photonic, solid-state lighting, chromaticity, directionality, spectral, angular, integrated photonic systems). Unscoped on the current wording the lexical condition did NOT return 715832 in its top-10 (lexical rank 1 was 896410 OPAN) while dense ranked it 2, hybrid 3 and hybrid_rerank 2. Scoped lexical rank 1 is uninformative because the scope holds only 10 projects, so every survivor ranks in every condition.

text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is to study working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
notes: Scope wording: 'whose stated aim is to study working memory' matches the filter's topic clause (objective or title), and deliberately excludes fellowships that merely ran a working-memory task while reporting - 655423 NIBSAD (stated aim: 'visuospatial attention and cognitive control processes'; tDCS working-memory task on eighteen healthy elderly in its report) and 844246 AGEING PLASTICITY (stated aim: prefrontal plasticity and resilience against cognitive ageing; retro-cue working memory task in its report) are out of scope by the question's own words. Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF; no MSCA-PF scheme exists in this corpus) AND working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (14 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - title states working memory control in aged bilinguals, MEG in young vs old adults, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - objective states the aim as enhancement of working memory capacity in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - title states decision-making and working memory in health and old age, extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-5 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 2, NeWMaBIL 5).

text: Among the MSCA-funded projects classified under inclusive education or special education, which ones collected their research data directly from large numbers of school students themselves, and how did their research designs differ?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle IN ('inclusive education','special education') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the six survivors did: IE2 (660607) and INCLUDed (101030992). IE2 ran its data collection inside schools - 'More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders' in Southern California, with data from two further European countries added during the first 24 months - and analysed it by combining advanced social network analysis with ethnographic methods to examine social interactions, friendships and peer relationships, with an emphasis on students identified as having special educational needs; its deliverables include a social network analysis toolkit for practitioners. INCLUDed collected data from a large nationally representative sample of 14-year-old lower-secondary students in Italy in order to develop, adapt and validate multifaceted measurement instruments for intercultural competence (IC) and for classroom cultural diversity climate (CCDC), the latter 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments', and then examined which culturally inclusive teaching approaches went with stronger IC. The designs differ in kind: IE2 is a school-based mixed network-and-ethnography study whose output is a practitioner toolkit, while INCLUDed is a large-scale quantitative instrument-development study whose output is validated measures plus evidence on teaching strategies.
notes: FILTER: purely structural - euroSciVoc leaf membership crossed with fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%'; unchanged since the first draft. Both leaves pass the one-reading check: SELECT DISTINCT euroSciVocPath, euroSciVocTitle, COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%inclusive education%' OR euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%special education%' GROUP BY 1,2 returns exactly two rows, 'social sciences/educational sciences/inclusive education' (10 projects) and 'social sciences/educational sciences/special education' (10), each a leaf, so title reading = subtree reading. Union of the two leaves is 19 projects (660607 carries both tags); crossing with MSCA leaves 6 survivors. No text/topic predicate anywhere in filter_sql. TEXTUAL PREDICATE: the project's own research data were collected directly from school students, in large numbers. Each conjunct is stated in both gold texts. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=6, every survivor read incl. workPerformed/finalResults): 660607 IE2 IN - 'Data collection from schools in Southern California has been completed. More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders'; 'data from two additional European countries have been collected during the first 24 months'. 101030992 INCLUDed IN - 'collected data from a large representative sample of lower-secondary students'; instrument for classroom cultural diversity climate 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments'; sample described in the objective as 'a large nationally representative sample of young people (14-year-olds) in a European country (i.e. Italy)'. 747083 MedLitRefYouth OUT - participants are not school students and are not numerous: '56 unaccompanied refugee children were interviewed', recruited 'By working with NGOs, volunteers and municipalities' in Italy and Sweden. 777720 CybSPEED OUT - no data collected from students: 'The grounds for sound experimental research have been laid, with some experiments already under way'; outputs are a theoretical framework, CPS models and Lattice Computing methods. 845783 ASSESSnet OUT - 'The data was principally collected by means of an online questionnaire and interviews with teachers involved in VM'; respondents are tertiary-level teachers. 101008184 xFORMAL OUT - work performed is scenario identification, a pathway editor, game mockups and feasibility tests of trails; no student data collection at all. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text) surfaced text-satisfying projects that fail the filter: 101018401 INCLUSION (ERC-ADG, euroSciVoc political economy|human migrations - 'We launched the Mitigation Study in the 2021-2022 academic year, covering over 20,000 students from 65 middle schools in Diyarbakir, Turkey ... collecting data from students via tablets'), 101004653 Inclusion4Schools (CSA, democracy|ethnology - 'A comprehensive survey was carried out ... targeting 1,358 schools'), 749068 GENSEG (MSCA fellowship, no inclusive/special-education tag - 'Using secondary data of 2235 adolescents from SOEP'). So the filter is load-bearing. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records who a project's data came from or how its design was built; the filter alone returns six projects of which four are off-question. SCOPED RANKS (k=10, scope 6, current text): 101030992 lexical 1 / dense 1 / hybrid 1 / rerank 1; 660607 lexical 2 / dense 2 / hybrid 2 / rerank 2 - both gold top-2 in every condition, ahead of all four rejects. TERM_STYLE paraphrase: the textual half uses none of the gold texts' distinctive vocabulary ('social network analysis', 'friendship networks', 'special educational needs', 'intercultural competence', 'classroom cultural diversity climate', 'nationally representative sample'); the only verbatim overlap ('inclusive education' in IE2's title) sits in the scope half.

text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects whose abstract mentions autism, which ones carry out their experiments in a non-human species, and which species do they use?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%autis%' OR p.title ILIKE '%autis%') AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Nine of the 29 ERC Starting Grants whose abstract mentions autism run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data. Rodents dominate: THERAUTISM screens molecular targets and a gene-therapy vector in preclinical mouse models of ASD, REVERSEAUTISM pairs Slc7a5 and BCKDK mutant mice with human cerebral organoids, DisConn images the awake mouse and maps the mouse axonal connectome, SafeFate characterises Myt1l knockout mice alongside human induced neurons, and NEUROGOAL and MotivatedBehaviors both record from circuits in behaving mice. Three step outside rodents - HomeoBalanceExcInh dissects excitation/inhibition balance in Drosophila Kenyon cells, MultiSense records whole-brain activity in larval zebrafish, and Brain2Bee tests its dopamine model in the honey bee.
notes: Filter: fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' plus the '%autis%' text condition over objective and title, which is what makes the survivor set enumerable (29 survivors). The question's anchor is worded to describe exactly what the filter reads - the project's own abstract - so a project whose only autism tie is in its published report (e.g. 637591 NEURAL AS, whose report mentions 'autistic spectrum disorders' while its abstract does not) is outside the question as well as outside the survivor set. At the runtime the structured half carries only fundingScheme; the topical half falls to retrieval (scoped.py whitelists no subject-matter column). Adjudication was exhaustive: all 29 survivor objectives read, plus workPerformed/finalResults for every IN and borderline case, plus a survivor-scoped SQL species sweep (mouse/mice, rat/rodent, zebrafish, Drosophila/flies, honey bee, monkey/macaque/primate/ferret/C. elegans over objective + report text). The adjudication test is whether the project's own text shows it carrying out experiments in a named non-human species. IN (9): 639489 HomeoBalanceExcInh - Drosophila Kenyon-cell circuit, 'allowing flies to learn to discriminate between different odours'; 677878 NEUROGOAL - two-photon imaging in 'foraging mice' and a mouse model of autism; 715508 REVERSEAUTISM - 'Employing a series of mouse models', plus human cerebral organoids; 715980 MultiSense - 'brain-wide response of larval zebrafish'; 757583 Brain2Bee - 'an animal model, the honey bee'; 802371 DisConn - 'recordings in the awake mouse', 'mouse axonal connectome'; 804710 SafeFate - 'new Myt1l knockout mouse models'; 851231 THERAUTISM - 'the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD'; 949652 MotivatedBehaviors - 'I characterized in mice a novel circuit', mouse models of psychiatric disease. OUT (20): 636458 CogSoCoAGE, 676943 SLAB, 678286 CONTEXTVISION, 678733 CAASD, 679927 SYNAPLAST MR, 715824 POINTS, 716974 Becoming Social, 755816 AUTISMS, 801708 ANTICIPATE, 801715 PUPILTRAITS, 804881 NEUROEPIGENETHICS, 852570 CoCoFlex, 852885 INDIVISUAL, 853211 DEVCOM, 946228 DEFEND, 948545 TrackingMinds, 950010 FamilySleeps - human participants, human cohorts, human imaging/gaze/pupillometry data, algorithms or ethics work, with no species keyword anywhere in objective or report text; plus three that do experimental biology without ever showing an experiment in a named species - 716011 NANOGLU ('synaptic proteins endogenously expressed in neurons'), 950013 CERCODE ('models of early cerebellar disruptions'), and 803984 GIDE, whose only species word in the whole record is the abstract's closing CV clause 'my extensive training in viral and mouse genetic techniques' while all four report sections (lineage barcoding, single-cell transcriptomics, membrane-potential perturbation) name no organism. Discrimination counter-examples (satisfy the text, fail the ERC-STG filter): 899727 DUPDOWN (ERC-POC) 'brain organoids and in vivo models' for ASD; 660259 OPTOFRAX (MSCA-IF-EF-RI) 'Optopharmacological brain mapping of autism mouse models'; 845065 CANSAS (MSCA-IF) 'fMRI in rodents and humans' for autism subtypes; 700999 NMDARETT (MSCA-IF); 799164 ProTeAN (MSCA-IF-EF-RI); 844318 NeuroTick (MSCA-IF). term_style = paraphrase: the discriminating vocabulary ('non-human species', 'carry out their experiments') appears nowhere in the gold texts, which say Drosophila/flies, foraging mice, larval zebrafish, honey bee, awake mouse, Myt1l knockout mouse models; only the topical anchor is close to the survivors' shared wording, and it is the filter-side anchor, not the discriminator. Scoped retrievability: the drafter's own k=20 scoped pooled run placed 6 of the accepted members in some condition's top-20; the independent reviewer's re-measurement with differently worded scoped queries reached 9 of 10 and then 10 of 10, so the shortfall was a property of one query wording, not of the cell.
